back: N, P, K, Ca, Mg and S: needed by plants in relatively large amounts.
Nutrients needed in tiny amounts, e.g. Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu, B, Mo; still essential.

front: Which nutrient deficiency shows as purpling of young maize leaves?
Sign of nitrogen deficiency in maize
back: Yellowing of older, lower leaves in a V from the tip down the midrib; stunted, pale plants.
Scorching (browning) of the margins of older leaves; weak stalks that lodge.
Interveinal chlorosis (stripes) on older leaves; Mg is the centre of chlorophyll.
Mobile (N, P, K, Mg) → symptoms on old leaves. Immobile (Ca, Fe, B, mostly S) → symptoms on young leaves and growing points.
Blossom-end rot of tomatoes; empty groundnut pods (pops); dead growing points.
Lush soft growth, lodging, more pests and diseases, late maturity, leaching and pollution, wasted money.
